page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.4-16 is a flexible virtual instance engineered for general compute tasks requiring consistent CPU throughput. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the machine utilizes an AMD EPYC 7J13 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.55 GHz. The configuration allocates 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, yielding 8 dedicated virtual CPUs. Dedicated CPU allocation ensures predictable thread scheduling without CPU contention from co-located virtual guests.

The instance is provisioned with 16.0 GB of system memory, which yields an allocation of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This 1:2 resource ratio establishes a compute-skewed footprint suitable for workloads with moderate caching and memory consumption. There is no bundled local storage on this instance, meaning all persistent data and operating system installations require network-attached storage volumes. For connectivity, the configuration provides one complimentary public IPv4 address, while hardware accelerators such as GPUs are not present.

With a 1:2 compute-to-memory profile and no native NVMe or disk storage, the primary tradeoff centers on memory density and external storage latency. The architecture prioritizes processing density per compute unit over large in-memory caches. VM.Standard.E4.Flex.4-16 is appropriate for stateless application servers, automated build and CI/CD pipelines, containerized microservices, distributed worker nodes, and batch computation tasks where data volumes do not require massive resident memory.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.4-16 is a flexible compute-focused virtual machine instance built on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7J13 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.55 GHz. It provisions 4 physical cores supporting simultaneous multithreading, providing 8 dedicated vCPUs alongside 16.0 GB of system memory. This configuration results in a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, aligning resource density toward compute-centric execution rather than memory-heavy datasets. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, necessitating remote block storage attachments for persistent filesystems, and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Without hardware GPU acceleration, the platform relies purely on its x86_64 CPU cores. VM.Standard.E4.Flex.4-16 fits workloads requiring steady CPU capacity with modest memory footprints, such as CI/CD runners, distributed build systems, backend microservices, web serving tiers, and batch processing utilities.
